auth_observations: No first-party Bearer or API key headers are visible on captured API calls; access to apik.carvana.io and apim.carvana.io is blocked by Cloudflare, so authenticated calls likely include additional headers or cookies not seen here.

CORS preflight OPTIONS requests to apik.carvana.io include Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization,content-type,correlation-context, indicating that actual POST calls carry an Authorization header and a correlation-context header for tracing.
All blocked API responses from apim.carvana.io and apik.carvana.io return Cloudflare HTML with no Set-Cookie or auth tokens, confirming that the blocking happens before app-level auth.

Google Identity Services (accounts.google.com gsi/fedcm.json and fedcm/listaccounts plus google.com/.well-known/web-identity) are used for optional Google One Tap sign-in, but no Carvana-specific auth token exchange is visible in this capture.

Most analytics and tracking endpoints (analytics.carvana.io, pixels.spotify.com, t.getletterpress.com, bat.bing.com, analytics.audioeye.com, api.consentjs.datagrail.io) use anonymous or cookie-based tracking; no reusable API tokens are exposed in headers.
narrative:
484 total requests were captured across 20 hosts. Method distribution is POST 191, OPTIONS 168, GET 125. Using host and path heuristics, roughly 290 requests are clear noise (analytics beacons, static assets, CDNs, tracking pixels, Cloudflare challenges). The remaining ~190 are to Carvana business APIs and HTML navigation endpoints.

The most important business APIs are under apik.carvana.io and apim.carvana.io. However, Cloudflare blocked access to these APIs from the capture environment, so nearly all calls to these hosts are either OPTIONS preflight requests or 403 HTML responses. Despite this, the URL patterns and query parameters clearly reveal the intended API surface.

For the user task of browsing/searching inventory and inspecting a specific vehicle, the main high-interest endpoints are:
- apik.carvana.io/merch/search/api/v2/search (POST): the core search endpoint for the SRP, taking a JSON body (not visible) and returning matching vehicles.
- apik.carvana.io/merch/search/api/v2/search/facets (POST): complementary endpoint returning facets/filters for the current search.
- apik.carvana.io/merch/search/api/v2/pricing (POST): returns pricing information for vehicles on the SRP.
- apim.carvana.io/vehicle-details-api/api/v1/vehicledetails (GET): the primary vehicle details API for a given vehicleId; this is the main endpoint for VDP data, though the single captured request returns a Cloudflare block page.
- Several supporting vehicle endpoints on apik.carvana.io/merch/vehicledetails (availability, inspection report, recall) and merchui/servicecontracts plus apimpub GapWaiver for add-on products.

These patterns indicate a fairly standard separation: apik.carvana.io hosts merchandising/search and vehicle-detail microservices, while apim.carvana.io hosts a composite vehicle-details-api. The capture includes one GET to apim.carvana.io/vehicle-details-api/api/v1/vehicledetails?vehicleId=4195259 which is the clearest candidate for "main API endpoint that returns the data needed" for a vehicle details page. For search results, /merch/search/api/v2/search is the core data provider, with facets and pricing as adjuncts.

Auth-wise, no Bearer tokens or explicit API keys appear in the captured headers, likely because Cloudflare blocked the calls before they reached app-level authentication. CORS preflights to apik.carvana.io request authorization and correlation-context headers, strongly suggesting that real POST requests include an Authorization header (probably a JWT or opaque token) plus a correlation ID. Google Identity Services FedCM endpoints are present for optional Google One Tap sign-in, but no downstream Carvana auth token exchange is visible.

Most other endpoints are low-interest analytics and tracking: analytics.carvana.io's web-eventable/graph and split-test APIs, Snowplow at t.getletterpress.com, Spotify pixels, Bing and Google Ads beacons, AudioEye accessibility analytics, and ConsentJS. Static asset manifests and spinner data live on static.fastly.carvana.io, assets.fastly.carvana.io, storage.googleapis.com, and spinnerdata.carvana.io.

In summary, the capture is heavily impacted by Cloudflare blocking, but still reveals the primary Carvana APIs. For automation, the key endpoints are apim.carvana.io/vehicle-details-api/api/v1/vehicledetails for detailed vehicle data and apik.carvana.io/merch/search/api/v2/search (plus facets and pricing) for search results. Any real automation against these endpoints will need to replicate whatever auth and anti-bot mechanisms Carvana uses (likely cookies, Authorization headers, and Cloudflare challenges), which are not fully observable in this trace.
